Both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False` and DRF only runs `validate_<field>` for fields present in the input, so a report with neither field validates successfully; there is no object-level `validate()` on BrowserReportSerializer.

gen_request_data compares `error_events[i]["timestamp"]` (nodestore event data, unix seconds) against `event.get("timestamp")` from rrweb frames, which testutils explicitly documents as milliseconds, so the while-condition is always true and every error is emitted before the first breadcrumb. Both renderDefaultHeadCell and renderDefaultBodyCell use `const cell = render...?.(...); if (cell) return cell;`. The stories document the contract as 'if the function returns undefined, fallback renderer will run', so `0`, `''`, `false` and `null` returns silently fall through to the default renderer.

The hook uses `projectIds: projectIds ?? selection.projects` — the provided prop wins, and the only caller passes `projectIds: projects`. Falling back to page filters when the prop is absent is the documented behaviour of UseTraceItemAttributeBaseProps.

The old useApiQuery call passed `retry: false`; the new plain useQuery passes only `enabled`, and DEFAULT_QUERY_CLIENT_CONFIG sets only refetchOnReconnect/refetchOnWindowFocus, so react-query v5's default of 3 retries now applies.

On react-query v5 a disabled query has status 'pending', so `isPending` is true and the hook returns early before touching `data`; the `isPending`/`isError` guards also narrow UseQueryResult's discriminated union, which is why `data.summary` type-checks.

The validation loop `return`s a 422 on the first invalid report, so the already-valid reports earlier in the same array are dropped and the browser will retry the whole batch — a poor fit for an endpoint whose stated purpose is observing real-world browser data.
